1	---
2	name: status-report
3	description: >-
4	  Build the every-two-weeks Applied Performance status report for Kenny Boyd and Chris
5	  Ruf — paste-ready email, one-page PDF, internal record. Use when the user says
6	  "/status-report", "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly
7	  update", "status update for Chris and Kenny", "what do I send Chris this week", or
8	  when a scheduled report date arrives. Do not use for a single meeting brief (use
9	  meeting-prep) or the end-of-day supervisor log interview (use interview-me).
10	---
11	
12	# Status Report
13	
14	Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report — an email to **Kenny Boyd and
15	Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly ("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), every two weeks, ~270 words.
16	
17	Governed by **KR 4.1** in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3). Read that KR as a
18	**content checklist** — shipped work, work in flight, decisions needed, anything at risk,
19	what's next — not as a layout. Eric's real reports run as flat prose with no section
20	headers. See **Voice** below; match it.
21	
22	**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
23	needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
24	sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
25	for; do not let it slip out of the output.
26	
27	**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
28	interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.
29	
30	## Paths
31	
32	Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` for all paths — never hardcode. Keys used
33	here: `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`,
34	`vault_status_reports`, `vault_status_log`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_scoreboard`,
35	`okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`.
36	
37	Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
38	Output dir: `{vault_status_reports}`
39	
40	> Each machine has its own config: `config.windows.json` holds `C:\Users\eric_rash\...`
41	> paths (correct on Windows), `config.macos.json` holds `/Users/kristinarash/...` paths.
42	> Read the one for the machine you are on. If its values point at the *other* machine's
43	> layout, or `vault_root` does not exist, stop and fix the config first — every skill that
44	> trusts it is broken until you do. (Until 2026-08-11 a single config held stale Windows
45	> paths; the split per-platform configs replaced it.)
46	
47	## Relationship to other skills
48	
49	- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
50	  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
51	  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
52	  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
53	- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
54	  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
55	  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
56	- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Step 1 — Establish the period
61	
62	Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
63	`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.
64	
65	**Count sends.** KR 4.1's target is "≥3 **sent** by Aug 31," and writing a file is not
66	sending it. Count files in `{vault_status_reports}` with `sent: true` in frontmatter —
67	that is the real number. Report progress toward ≥3 in Step 8. If files exist with
68	`sent: false` older than a week, ask whether they actually went out; an uncounted send
69	is as bad for the KR as a missed one.
70	
71	A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
72	archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.
73	
74	**Cadence is settled: every two weeks.** Eric committed to it in writing in the first
75	report — "Starting these updates every two weeks." Report 1 went out **2026-08-24**, so
76	sends land on even fortnights from there (2026-09-07, 09-21, 10-05, …). The earlier
77	"twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday" plan was an assistant assumption and is retired.
78	
79	## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)
80	
81	### Step 2a — Preflight the meeting source
82	
83	Run `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5` first.
84	
85	**Fixed 2026-08-11** — the key is in `~/.zshrc` and the local mirror was rebuilt with
86	`fireflies-pp-cli sync`; as of 2026-08-13 the key is visible to the Bash tool directly.
87	The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`, not `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/`.
88	
89	If it fails again, `unable to open database file: out of memory (14)` means the mirror is
90	**missing, not corrupt** — run `sync` before anything else. Then:
91	
92	- **Do not hard-stop.** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure; this skill must not,
93	  or it inherits the outage that already lapsed `weekly-review`.
94	- **Fall back** to reading `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` filtered to the period by the
95	  `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename prefix. These files have **no YAML frontmatter** — parse the
96	  prepended header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) and the
97	  Fireflies export sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
98	- **Check staleness and say so.** Compare the newest meeting file's date to today. If
99	  the gap is >2 days, tell the user plainly in Step 8: *"Meeting data is stale through
100	  {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."* A silently incomplete
101	  report is worse than a flagged one — the user is about to send it to a supervisor.
102	- Record the degraded source in the internal record's frontmatter.
103	
104	### Step 2b — Pull
105	
106	Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.
107	
108	1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
109	   (flags verified valid; `--since` accepts `7d`/`24h` form). Gives titles, gists,
110	   topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}`.
111	   On failure, use the 2a fallback.
112	1b. **Supervisor logs — read these before anything else.** Every file in
113	   `{vault_status_log}` whose `YYYY-MM-DD.md` filename falls inside the period. These are
114	   written by `closeout` Step 0 (or `interview-me` Part 0) and they are the **highest-value source in
115	   this step**: they cover equipment, installs, hallway conversations, and follow-ups
116	   awaiting a reply — the operational two thirds that appears in no other source. Merge
117	   the three sections (`## Equipment & installs`, `## People & conversations`,
118	   `## Waiting on / risks`) across the period and union every `sports:` array for the
119	   coverage panel.
120	
121	   Treat the wording as the user's own and preserve it. **Count the logged days** —
122	   `logged / days-in-period` gets reported in Step 8. A thin count is not a reason to
123	   pad; it is the number that tells the user the nightly ritual lapsed.
124	
125	   Zero logs is normal for now and is **never** a hard stop — the ritual started
126	   2026-09-07 and the report predates it. Fall back to a full Step 4 interview.
127	
128	2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
129	   (`--from` takes an integer number of days). Flag anything open >14 days; those are
130	   risk-section candidates. On failure, parse `## Action items` blocks from the vault
131	   meeting files instead.
132	
133	   **Known broken as of 2026-09-07:** this command exits 0 and returns an array of empty
134	   `{}` objects — a serialization bug, not an empty result. Do not read it as "no open
135	   commitments." The digest in item 1 carries action items inline; use those and record
136	   the degraded source in the internal record.
137	3. **Shipped artifacts** — read `{vault_output_ledger}`, newest first, entries within
138	   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**
139	
140	   Format is a markdown table, newest first, data rows starting at line 22:
141	   `| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |` where *Shipped* is `YYYY-MM-DD`,
142	   *Artifact* is the short name, *What it is* is a dense paragraph, and *Harvest* holds
143	   `[[wikilinks]]` or is empty. Match rows with `^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by
144	   date. Compress *What it is* to one clause for the email — those paragraphs run long
145	   and will blow the 300-word ceiling if pasted whole.
146	4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
147	   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
148	5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs). This is the **only** trustworthy KR
149	   source. Two others will lie to you:
150	
151	   - **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — superseded v2 set of 9.
152	   - **Do not trust `{okr_scoreboard}` for confidence values.** It was generated
153	     2026-06-12 against the retired *quarterly, 3-objective* set and scores KRs that no
154	     longer exist; v3's fourth objective (Leadership & Visibility) isn't in it at all.
155	     Its `Conf` decimals are real numbers attached to dead targets. If it still predates
156	     the v3 restructure (2026-07-17), tell the user it needs regenerating — `okrs.yaml`
157	     is the source of truth, `okr.py` regenerates `SCOREBOARD.md` and `okrs.json` — and
158	     report KR status from `{okr_doc}` alone in the meantime.
159	
160	6. **Sport roster** — the 17-program list for the coverage panel comes from
161	   `{utilization_brief}` §"Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the two XC / Track &
162	   Field rows each bundle two programs). Never re-derive this list from memory. Note it
163	   is *prescriptive* — what each program could use — not a record of current activity,
164	   which is exactly why the coverage panel is worth publishing.
165	7. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
166	   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
167	8. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.
168	
169	### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage
170	
171	`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
172	outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
173	sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
174	never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
175	stage feeds *In Progress*.
176	
177	## Voice — match the real thing, not the spec
178	
179	**Read `{vault_status_reports}/2026-08-24-email-sent.txt` before drafting.** That is the
180	first report Eric actually sent. It is the reference for how he writes; this skill's
181	earlier draft was never sent and should not be imitated.
182	
183	What his email actually does:
184	
185	- **No section headers.** Flat short paragraphs, one topic each, no Shipped / In Progress
186	  / Decisions Needed labels. Do not impose the KR 4.1 headers on his prose — they are the
187	  *content checklist*, not the layout. Make sure each of the five things is covered
188	  somewhere; do not label them.
189	- **One framing line up top**, then straight into it. No preamble.
190	- **"We" for department work, "I" for his own actions.** He writes as the unit.
191	- **Concrete and operational.** Equipment, buildings, people, dates: Perch cameras at
192	  Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar, survey cutoff August 28th. Names people
193	  freely — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi, Micah.
194	- **Asks come last and land soft:** "One ask I wanted to run past you both is whether…"
195	  Do **not** convert these into "need Chris by Aug 31." That register is more forceful
196	  than he writes and it will read as someone else's words.
197	- **Stalled things get passed along, not escalated:** "still haven't heard back. Passing
198	  that along in case a nudge is warranted."
199	- **About 270 words. No attachment.** The memo PDF exists for when something needs to be
200	  handed across a table; the ordinary cycle is email only.
201	
202	### The sourcing gap this exposed — important
203	
204	Almost nothing in his real report appears in `portfolio.json` or `_ledger.md`: survey
205	response rates, camera installs at three buildings, heart-rate monitors arriving for
206	tennis, staff meeting cadence, a stalled email to Micah. Those sources track his
207	**building** work. He reports his **departmental operations**.
208	
209	So the auto-pull covers maybe a third of what belongs in the report. **Weight the
210	interview accordingly** — ask about equipment, deliveries, installs, staffing, meetings
211	held, and follow-ups awaiting a reply, not just what moved in the registry. Treat a draft
212	built only from automated sources as roughly one-third finished.
213	
214	## Step 3 — Draft before asking
215	
216	Write a complete draft of all five sections from the pull. Cut to **5–6 projects with
217	real motion** — never a 14-line roster. Projects that didn't move go to the internal
218	record and, if relevant, the sport coverage panel.
219	
220	Tag every Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*,
221	*(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*.
222	
223	Then identify the gaps — that is what the interview is for.
224	
225	## Step 4 — Interview the gaps only
226	
227	Ask in **one batch**, not serially. Keep it to what the pull genuinely couldn't answer.
228	Lead with targeted gap questions, then the four standing ones.
229	
230	**Targeted** (generated from the pull, examples):
231	- "Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything from them that Chris needs?"
232	- "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period — is that right, or did something go out
233	  that never got logged?"
234	- "Kinexon_Volleyball hasn't moved in the registry since July. Stalled, or just not
235	  logged?"
236	
237	**Skip every standing question the supervisor logs already answered.** If
238	`{vault_status_log}` covered the period, questions 1–4 below are largely pre-filled —
239	read the merged log back to the user as a list and ask only *"anything missing?"* plus
240	questions 5–8. Re-asking what the user already typed at 9pm is how the nightly ritual
241	gets abandoned; the payoff for logging has to be a visibly shorter interview.
242	
243	**Standing** (every time). The first three carry most of the report — they cover the
244	operational half no automated source sees:
245	
246	1. **Equipment, installs, deliveries.** What arrived, what got installed where, what's
247	   being phased out, who's onboarding onto it. Eric's real reports lead with this
248	   (Perch cameras at Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar for tennis).
249	2. **Meetings held and staffing.** Who he met with, what came out of it, changes to
250	   cadence or who attends. Names matter — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi.
251	3. **Conversations no transcript caught** — hallway, text, sideline, phone. Invisible to
252	   every automated source, and among the highest-value things this interview captures.
253	4. **Anything waiting on someone else.** Unanswered emails, pending approvals, stalled
254	   follow-ups. These become the soft "passing that along" lines at the end.
255	5. **Anything about to go sideways** that Chris and Kenny should hear from him first.
256	   *(Push here. An always-empty risk line means it isn't being used honestly.)*
257	6. **Any ask** — time at a meeting, a decision, a nudge. Phrased softly, at the end.
258	7. **Ideas generated** — worth parking, pitching, or building?
259	8. **What's next** for the coming two weeks.
260	
261	Also ask, if the pull shows thin coverage: *"Any sport you touched this period that
262	isn't showing up in my sources?"* Non-revenue involvement is the whole point and it is
263	the most likely thing to be undercounted.
264	
265	## Step 5 — Assemble and check
266	
267	Fill the template at `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`.
268	
269	Run every check before showing the user anything:
270	
271	- [ ] **Email body is under 300 words.** Count it. State the count. Over the ceiling,
272	      cut — do not negotiate with yourself.
273	- [ ] **Every Shipped line traces to a `_ledger.md` entry.** No exceptions.
274	- [ ] **No endorsement claimed that doesn't exist.** If sign-off is pending, "our
275	      standard intake process," never "the approved process."
276	- [ ] **Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag.**
277	- [ ] **Every Decisions Needed item names a person and a date.** No owner or no date
278	      means it isn't a decision request — rewrite or cut it.
279	- [ ] **Jargon table enforced.** No CMJ, ACWR, asymmetry index, unexplained B.A.I.R.
280	- [ ] **Department names.** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning / S&C),
281	      Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science).
282	- [ ] **Never "one unified dashboard."** The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke
283	      on top."
284	- [ ] **Research presented as research** — no readiness or deployment claims.
285	- [ ] **Risks section is non-empty** unless the user explicitly confirmed there's
286	      nothing. Ask once more before letting it go empty.
287	- [ ] **Repeat check:** any Decisions Needed item carried over from the previous report
288	      gets flagged to the user — two unanswered asks means the email has failed at it
289	      and it needs raising in person.
290	- [ ] **Email and PDF agree.** The two are filled separately, so verify it: every
291	      Shipped, In Progress, Decisions Needed, and Risks item in the email appears in the
292	      PDF. The PDF may carry *more* detail — it must never carry different facts, a
293	      different sport tag, or a different date. Sending a supervisor two versions of the
294	      same report is the failure this check exists to prevent.
295	- [ ] **Sport coverage panel is not padded.** Untouched sports stay marked untouched. A
296	      thin panel is real information; a padded one destroys the evidentiary value of
297	      every honest panel before and after it.
298	
299	**Loop until clean.** Any failed box: fix the draft, then run the whole list again from
300	the top — a cut for word count can drop a sport tag or the only risk line. Show the user
301	the draft only after one full pass with every box ticked.
302	
303	## Step 6 — Emit
304	
305	Produce three things:
306	
307	1. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record, full Layer 3
308	   structure from the template: email as sent, meetings held, conversations, ideas, full
309	   roster, KR ledger, and the "Not for the report" candid section.
310	2. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — render
311	   `assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content. One page, always.
312	
313	   **It is a printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Single column, one serif family,
314	   letterspaced small-cap section heads, one green hairline. Never reintroduce status
315	   dots, badge or pill rows, bolded stat lines, progress bars, or a two-column grid —
316	   that vocabulary is what made the first version read as generated.
317	
318	   **Measure before shipping**, don't eyeball it. Budget is **950px of content at 666px
319	   width**:
320	
321	   Same script on both machines (`python3` on the Mac, `python` on Windows); it finds
322	   Chrome and the temp folder itself:
323	
324	   ```python
325	   import pathlib, platform, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile
326	   html = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])            # the one-pager .html
327	   chrome = {"Darwin": "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome",
328	             "Windows": r"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"}[platform.system()]
329	   probe = pathlib.Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "probe.html"
330	   probe.write_text(html.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("</body>",
331	       '<script>window.addEventListener("load",()=>{document.title='
332	       '"H:"+Math.round(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)})</script></body>'),
333	       encoding="utf-8")
334	   dom = subprocess.run([chrome, "--headless", "--disable-gpu", "--virtual-time-budget=3000",
335	                         "--window-size=666,1200", "--dump-dom", probe.as_uri()],
336	                        capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
337	                        errors="replace").stdout   # Windows Python defaults to cp1252
338	   print(re.search(r"<title>H:(\d+)", dom).group(1), "px (budget 950)")
339	   ```
340	
341	   Then render with the same `chrome`: `--headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer
342	   --print-to-pdf=<out> <html file URI>` (or the `html-to-pdf` skill on Windows).
343	   Over 950px, **cut prose** — never drop below 9.6pt. This gets printed and read by
344	   people who will not squint for you.
345	3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
346	   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
347	   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
348	   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
349	   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
350	   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
351	4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
352	   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.
353	
354	### Do not send
355	
356	The connected Gmail account is the user's **personal** address
357	(`eric.rash11@gmail.com`), not Baylor. Do not create Gmail drafts — they would land in
358	the wrong mailbox. The user sends from Outlook on the work account.
359	
360	Never send a report to a supervisor without the user reading it first, under any
361	circumstance.
362	
363	## Step 7 — Log
364	
365	- Append shipped artifacts to `{vault_output_ledger}` if the interview surfaced any that
366	  weren't logged.
367	- Update `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` with confirmed status, sport, and KR
368	  mapping — this keeps the canonical spine current as a byproduct rather than a chore.
369	- Add an `updates[]` entry to `{portfolio_json}` for each project reported as moved, via
370	  the `project` skill, so the registry stops being empty.
371	- Set `sent: false` in the internal record. The user flips it after sending.
372	
373	## Step 8 — Report to the user
374	
375	State: word count, report number, next send date, which sports appeared, anything the
376	checks flagged, and where the three files landed.
377	
378	Also state **`N of D` days logged** in `{vault_status_log}` for the period. Say it
379	plainly and without nagging — the number is the nudge. When the count is low, say what it
380	cost: *"6 of 14 days logged, so the interview had to cover the other 8 from memory."*
381

---
name: status-report
description: >-
  Build the every-two-weeks Applied Performance status report for Kenny Boyd and Chris
  Ruf — paste-ready email, one-page PDF, internal record. Use when the user says
  "/status-report", "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly
  update", "status update for Chris and Kenny", "what do I send Chris this week", or
  when a scheduled report date arrives. Do not use for a single meeting brief (use
  meeting-prep) or the end-of-day supervisor log interview (use interview-me).
---

# Status Report

Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report — an email to **Kenny Boyd and
Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly ("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), every two weeks, ~270 words.

Governed by **KR 4.1** in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3). Read that KR as a
**content checklist** — shipped work, work in flight, decisions needed, anything at risk,
what's next — not as a layout. Eric's real reports run as flat prose with no section
headers. See **Voice** below; match it.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
for; do not let it slip out of the output.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` for all paths — never hardcode. Keys used
here: `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`,
`vault_status_reports`, `vault_status_log`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_scoreboard`,
`okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`.

Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
Output dir: `{vault_status_reports}`

> Each machine has its own config: `config.windows.json` holds `C:\Users\eric_rash\...`
> paths (correct on Windows), `config.macos.json` holds `/Users/kristinarash/...` paths.
> Read the one for the machine you are on. If its values point at the *other* machine's
> layout, or `vault_root` does not exist, stop and fix the config first — every skill that
> trusts it is broken until you do. (Until 2026-08-11 a single config held stale Windows
> paths; the split per-platform configs replaced it.)

## Relationship to other skills

- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.

---

## Step 1 — Establish the period

Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.

**Count sends.** KR 4.1's target is "≥3 **sent** by Aug 31," and writing a file is not
sending it. Count files in `{vault_status_reports}` with `sent: true` in frontmatter —
that is the real number. Report progress toward ≥3 in Step 8. If files exist with
`sent: false` older than a week, ask whether they actually went out; an uncounted send
is as bad for the KR as a missed one.

A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.

**Cadence is settled: every two weeks.** Eric committed to it in writing in the first
report — "Starting these updates every two weeks." Report 1 went out **2026-08-24**, so
sends land on even fortnights from there (2026-09-07, 09-21, 10-05, …). The earlier
"twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday" plan was an assistant assumption and is retired.

## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)

### Step 2a — Preflight the meeting source

Run `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5` first.

**Fixed 2026-08-11** — the key is in `~/.zshrc` and the local mirror was rebuilt with
`fireflies-pp-cli sync`; as of 2026-08-13 the key is visible to the Bash tool directly.
The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`, not `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/`.

If it fails again, `unable to open database file: out of memory (14)` means the mirror is
**missing, not corrupt** — run `sync` before anything else. Then:

- **Do not hard-stop.** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure; this skill must not,
  or it inherits the outage that already lapsed `weekly-review`.
- **Fall back** to reading `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` filtered to the period by the
  `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename prefix. These files have **no YAML frontmatter** — parse the
  prepended header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) and the
  Fireflies export sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
- **Check staleness and say so.** Compare the newest meeting file's date to today. If
  the gap is >2 days, tell the user plainly in Step 8: *"Meeting data is stale through
  {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."* A silently incomplete
  report is worse than a flagged one — the user is about to send it to a supervisor.
- Record the degraded source in the internal record's frontmatter.

### Step 2b — Pull

Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.

1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
   (flags verified valid; `--since` accepts `7d`/`24h` form). Gives titles, gists,
   topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}`.
   On failure, use the 2a fallback.
1b. **Supervisor logs — read these before anything else.** Every file in
   `{vault_status_log}` whose `YYYY-MM-DD.md` filename falls inside the period. These are
   written by `closeout` Step 0 (or `interview-me` Part 0) and they are the **highest-value source in
   this step**: they cover equipment, installs, hallway conversations, and follow-ups
   awaiting a reply — the operational two thirds that appears in no other source. Merge
   the three sections (`## Equipment & installs`, `## People & conversations`,
   `## Waiting on / risks`) across the period and union every `sports:` array for the
   coverage panel.

   Treat the wording as the user's own and preserve it. **Count the logged days** —
   `logged / days-in-period` gets reported in Step 8. A thin count is not a reason to
   pad; it is the number that tells the user the nightly ritual lapsed.

   Zero logs is normal for now and is **never** a hard stop — the ritual started
   2026-09-07 and the report predates it. Fall back to a full Step 4 interview.

2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
   (`--from` takes an integer number of days). Flag anything open >14 days; those are
   risk-section candidates. On failure, parse `## Action items` blocks from the vault
   meeting files instead.

   **Known broken as of 2026-09-07:** this command exits 0 and returns an array of empty
   `{}` objects — a serialization bug, not an empty result. Do not read it as "no open
   commitments." The digest in item 1 carries action items inline; use those and record
   the degraded source in the internal record.
3. **Shipped artifacts** — read `{vault_output_ledger}`, newest first, entries within
   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**

   Format is a markdown table, newest first, data rows starting at line 22:
   `| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |` where *Shipped* is `YYYY-MM-DD`,
   *Artifact* is the short name, *What it is* is a dense paragraph, and *Harvest* holds
   `[[wikilinks]]` or is empty. Match rows with `^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by
   date. Compress *What it is* to one clause for the email — those paragraphs run long
   and will blow the 300-word ceiling if pasted whole.
4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs). This is the **only** trustworthy KR
   source. Two others will lie to you:

   - **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — superseded v2 set of 9.
   - **Do not trust `{okr_scoreboard}` for confidence values.** It was generated
     2026-06-12 against the retired *quarterly, 3-objective* set and scores KRs that no
     longer exist; v3's fourth objective (Leadership & Visibility) isn't in it at all.
     Its `Conf` decimals are real numbers attached to dead targets. If it still predates
     the v3 restructure (2026-07-17), tell the user it needs regenerating — `okrs.yaml`
     is the source of truth, `okr.py` regenerates `SCOREBOARD.md` and `okrs.json` — and
     report KR status from `{okr_doc}` alone in the meantime.

6. **Sport roster** — the 17-program list for the coverage panel comes from
   `{utilization_brief}` §"Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the two XC / Track &
   Field rows each bundle two programs). Never re-derive this list from memory. Note it
   is *prescriptive* — what each program could use — not a record of current activity,
   which is exactly why the coverage panel is worth publishing.
7. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
8. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.

### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage

`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
stage feeds *In Progress*.

## Voice — match the real thing, not the spec

**Read `{vault_status_reports}/2026-08-24-email-sent.txt` before drafting.** That is the
first report Eric actually sent. It is the reference for how he writes; this skill's
earlier draft was never sent and should not be imitated.

What his email actually does:

- **No section headers.** Flat short paragraphs, one topic each, no Shipped / In Progress
  / Decisions Needed labels. Do not impose the KR 4.1 headers on his prose — they are the
  *content checklist*, not the layout. Make sure each of the five things is covered
  somewhere; do not label them.
- **One framing line up top**, then straight into it. No preamble.
- **"We" for department work, "I" for his own actions.** He writes as the unit.
- **Concrete and operational.** Equipment, buildings, people, dates: Perch cameras at
  Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar, survey cutoff August 28th. Names people
  freely — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi, Micah.
- **Asks come last and land soft:** "One ask I wanted to run past you both is whether…"
  Do **not** convert these into "need Chris by Aug 31." That register is more forceful
  than he writes and it will read as someone else's words.
- **Stalled things get passed along, not escalated:** "still haven't heard back. Passing
  that along in case a nudge is warranted."
- **About 270 words. No attachment.** The memo PDF exists for when something needs to be
  handed across a table; the ordinary cycle is email only.

### The sourcing gap this exposed — important

Almost nothing in his real report appears in `portfolio.json` or `_ledger.md`: survey
response rates, camera installs at three buildings, heart-rate monitors arriving for
tennis, staff meeting cadence, a stalled email to Micah. Those sources track his
**building** work. He reports his **departmental operations**.

So the auto-pull covers maybe a third of what belongs in the report. **Weight the
interview accordingly** — ask about equipment, deliveries, installs, staffing, meetings
held, and follow-ups awaiting a reply, not just what moved in the registry. Treat a draft
built only from automated sources as roughly one-third finished.

## Step 3 — Draft before asking

Write a complete draft of all five sections from the pull. Cut to **5–6 projects with
real motion** — never a 14-line roster. Projects that didn't move go to the internal
record and, if relevant, the sport coverage panel.

Tag every Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*,
*(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*.

Then identify the gaps — that is what the interview is for.

## Step 4 — Interview the gaps only

Ask in **one batch**, not serially. Keep it to what the pull genuinely couldn't answer.
Lead with targeted gap questions, then the four standing ones.

**Targeted** (generated from the pull, examples):
- "Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything from them that Chris needs?"
- "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period — is that right, or did something go out
  that never got logged?"
- "Kinexon_Volleyball hasn't moved in the registry since July. Stalled, or just not
  logged?"

**Skip every standing question the supervisor logs already answered.** If
`{vault_status_log}` covered the period, questions 1–4 below are largely pre-filled —
read the merged log back to the user as a list and ask only *"anything missing?"* plus
questions 5–8. Re-asking what the user already typed at 9pm is how the nightly ritual
gets abandoned; the payoff for logging has to be a visibly shorter interview.

**Standing** (every time). The first three carry most of the report — they cover the
operational half no automated source sees:

1. **Equipment, installs, deliveries.** What arrived, what got installed where, what's
   being phased out, who's onboarding onto it. Eric's real reports lead with this
   (Perch cameras at Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar for tennis).
2. **Meetings held and staffing.** Who he met with, what came out of it, changes to
   cadence or who attends. Names matter — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi.
3. **Conversations no transcript caught** — hallway, text, sideline, phone. Invisible to
   every automated source, and among the highest-value things this interview captures.
4. **Anything waiting on someone else.** Unanswered emails, pending approvals, stalled
   follow-ups. These become the soft "passing that along" lines at the end.
5. **Anything about to go sideways** that Chris and Kenny should hear from him first.
   *(Push here. An always-empty risk line means it isn't being used honestly.)*
6. **Any ask** — time at a meeting, a decision, a nudge. Phrased softly, at the end.
7. **Ideas generated** — worth parking, pitching, or building?
8. **What's next** for the coming two weeks.

Also ask, if the pull shows thin coverage: *"Any sport you touched this period that
isn't showing up in my sources?"* Non-revenue involvement is the whole point and it is
the most likely thing to be undercounted.

## Step 5 — Assemble and check

Fill the template at `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`.

Run every check before showing the user anything:

- [ ] **Email body is under 300 words.** Count it. State the count. Over the ceiling,
      cut — do not negotiate with yourself.
- [ ] **Every Shipped line traces to a `_ledger.md` entry.** No exceptions.
- [ ] **No endorsement claimed that doesn't exist.** If sign-off is pending, "our
      standard intake process," never "the approved process."
- [ ] **Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag.**
- [ ] **Every Decisions Needed item names a person and a date.** No owner or no date
      means it isn't a decision request — rewrite or cut it.
- [ ] **Jargon table enforced.** No CMJ, ACWR, asymmetry index, unexplained B.A.I.R.
- [ ] **Department names.** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning / S&C),
      Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science).
- [ ] **Never "one unified dashboard."** The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke
      on top."
- [ ] **Research presented as research** — no readiness or deployment claims.
- [ ] **Risks section is non-empty** unless the user explicitly confirmed there's
      nothing. Ask once more before letting it go empty.
- [ ] **Repeat check:** any Decisions Needed item carried over from the previous report
      gets flagged to the user — two unanswered asks means the email has failed at it
      and it needs raising in person.
- [ ] **Email and PDF agree.** The two are filled separately, so verify it: every
      Shipped, In Progress, Decisions Needed, and Risks item in the email appears in the
      PDF. The PDF may carry *more* detail — it must never carry different facts, a
      different sport tag, or a different date. Sending a supervisor two versions of the
      same report is the failure this check exists to prevent.
- [ ] **Sport coverage panel is not padded.** Untouched sports stay marked untouched. A
      thin panel is real information; a padded one destroys the evidentiary value of
      every honest panel before and after it.

**Loop until clean.** Any failed box: fix the draft, then run the whole list again from
the top — a cut for word count can drop a sport tag or the only risk line. Show the user
the draft only after one full pass with every box ticked.

## Step 6 — Emit

Produce three things:

1. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record, full Layer 3
   structure from the template: email as sent, meetings held, conversations, ideas, full
   roster, KR ledger, and the "Not for the report" candid section.
2. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — render
   `assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content. One page, always.

   **It is a printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Single column, one serif family,
   letterspaced small-cap section heads, one green hairline. Never reintroduce status
   dots, badge or pill rows, bolded stat lines, progress bars, or a two-column grid —
   that vocabulary is what made the first version read as generated.

   **Measure before shipping**, don't eyeball it. Budget is **950px of content at 666px
   width**:

   Same script on both machines (`python3` on the Mac, `python` on Windows); it finds
   Chrome and the temp folder itself:

   ```python
   import pathlib, platform, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile
   html = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])            # the one-pager .html
   chrome = {"Darwin": "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome",
             "Windows": r"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"}[platform.system()]
   probe = pathlib.Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "probe.html"
   probe.write_text(html.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("</body>",
       '<script>window.addEventListener("load",()=>{document.title='
       '"H:"+Math.round(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)})</script></body>'),
       encoding="utf-8")
   dom = subprocess.run([chrome, "--headless", "--disable-gpu", "--virtual-time-budget=3000",
                         "--window-size=666,1200", "--dump-dom", probe.as_uri()],
                        capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
                        errors="replace").stdout   # Windows Python defaults to cp1252
   print(re.search(r"<title>H:(\d+)", dom).group(1), "px (budget 950)")
   ```

   Then render with the same `chrome`: `--headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer
   --print-to-pdf=<out> <html file URI>` (or the `html-to-pdf` skill on Windows).
   Over 950px, **cut prose** — never drop below 9.6pt. This gets printed and read by
   people who will not squint for you.
3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.

### Do not send

The connected Gmail account is the user's **personal** address
(`eric.rash11@gmail.com`), not Baylor. Do not create Gmail drafts — they would land in
the wrong mailbox. The user sends from Outlook on the work account.

Never send a report to a supervisor without the user reading it first, under any
circumstance.

## Step 7 — Log

- Append shipped artifacts to `{vault_output_ledger}` if the interview surfaced any that
  weren't logged.
- Update `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` with confirmed status, sport, and KR
  mapping — this keeps the canonical spine current as a byproduct rather than a chore.
- Add an `updates[]` entry to `{portfolio_json}` for each project reported as moved, via
  the `project` skill, so the registry stops being empty.
- Set `sent: false` in the internal record. The user flips it after sending.

## Step 8 — Report to the user

State: word count, report number, next send date, which sports appeared, anything the
checks flagged, and where the three files landed.

Also state **`N of D` days logged** in `{vault_status_log}` for the period. Say it
plainly and without nagging — the number is the nudge. When the count is low, say what it
cost: *"6 of 14 days logged, so the interview had to cover the other 8 from memory."*

**Propose a rule when one was missing.** If this run hit a problem no Step 5 box covers —
caught by you, or by Eric editing the draft before sending — end with one proposed new
checklist line and the reason. Add it to Step 5 only on Eric's yes; the next report is
then checked against it.

---

## Failure modes to design against

**Padding.** A thin period is a legitimate output. "Nothing shipped this period" is an
honest line that protects the word "shipped" everywhere else. Inflating a quiet period
is the fastest way to make the report worthless — and to make the time documentation
inadmissible when it matters.

**Roster creep.** The email is not a project list. 14 status lines reads as 14 things
half-done. Five moving projects reads as focus.

**The credit goal quietly disappearing.** The report exists so non-football,
non-basketball involvement becomes visible. If a period's coverage panel is thin, that
is real information and it should be shown, not hidden — a padded panel destroys the
evidentiary value of every honest one.

**Depending on another ritual.** `weekly-review` lapsed for seven weeks earlier this
year. This report must never require it.

in `SecondBrain/Projects/Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` — five sections
(Shipped / In Progress / Decisions Needed / Risks–No-Surprises / Next Two Weeks),

posts 3/27–10/5/2026, and 96 emails from Kenny to Eric (10/2025–10/5/2026), reviewed
2026-10-06.

**Two registers.** Agendas: bare outlines, two-sided slogans ("Thermostat vs.
Thermometer", "Anger vs. Apathy", "Be Present"), questions as prompts ("Why are we doing
___?"), a running "What I'm working on…" list repeated weekly. Posts: warm prose that
explains the reason for every ask.

**Post template.** Bold label-first title (PLEASE REVIEW: / ASSISTANCE NEEDED: /
REMINDER: / Article Review:), banner for big items → @team + one purpose sentence →
numbered asks to a role ("Unit Leads - Please…") → why → his travel/OOO dates → thanks.

**Tics.** Numbers in parentheses "(3) weeks", "(38)". Ellipses as hand-off ("Let us know
on this thread…"). Long sentences, typos left in — writes fast, substance over polish.
"We/us" by default; "I" when taking ownership. CAPS/bold only for rules with
consequences ("DO NOT PARK"). Light self-deprecating humor ("do forget (like I have)").

**Faith.** Woven in as allusion ("for such a time as this"), weekly Scripture + leadership
quote in fall 2025 agendas, "Spiritual Wellness day", prayer question in athlete survey.

**Bad-news pattern (4/30 Athletes.org post).** State headline neutrally → "dig into the
details" (asks sample size) → numbered context → concede ("We certainly can improve") →
name who owns it (Doug, Jovan, Dave Harper) → close on pride and mission. Defends team
without dismissing the criticism.

**Values.** Prep before meetings (bullets in advance). Lead time upward: internal
deadline well before the official one, so Doug/President have room. Explicit about who
sees what (Real Response access list). Good-neighbor framing; reframes constraints as
fortune. Protects staff time and well-being. Personnel requests go to him first, keep
him copied. Prefers subtraction over adding process. Skeptical of low-n surveys
("number of participants matter significantly").

SEPARATELY / FEEDBACK REQUESTED. Says exactly how to reply (reply all, separately,
text). Closes loopholes in asks ("(3) challenges; if personnel is one, give (3)
others"). Acks are one line ("Received. Thank you"). Credits people by name, often
including partner offices ("would not have been possible without…"). Tailors one
announcement for different audiences. To vendors: courteous, states his authority, makes no commitment.
Hospitality is a core value ("Unreasonable Hospitality" book for new staff).

and his review window ("by EOD Friday so I can review over the weekend"), with constraints

workflows rather than parallel ones. Approves with conditions (get the coach and AT to
sign off) and always "keep me updated," especially on cross-office comms. Delegates
by relationship ("you can speak their language to ITS"). Since 10/1/26: weekly
30-minute project check-in with Eric through the fall.

name: kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences
description: "Kenny Boyd's editorial constraints on Athletics policy/framework docs — no language implying past incompetence, no judgmental tier labels, name the seniority of reviewers"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 126c5de4-d928-4658-88d2-1922d2464a29
  modified: 2026-10-28T21:15:11.442Z
---

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

Format (his own words, Tech Sync 2026-10-28): no long wordy documents; "economy of
words"; a clean cover with the details behind it; charts and trend lines over
text ("not a pre-K version" either). Say plainly when something already exists
("we already have this") so work is not duplicated. To him "the SOP" means the
Software and Technology Management Framework.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

Format (his own words, Tech Sync 2026-10-28): no long wordy documents; "economy of
words"; a clean cover with the details behind it; charts and trend lines over
text ("not a pre-K version" either). Say plainly when something already exists
("we already have this") so work is not duplicated. To him "the SOP" means the
Software and Technology Management Framework.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: status-report
3	description: >-
4	  Build the every-two-weeks Applied Performance status report for Kenny Boyd and Chris
5	  Ruf — paste-ready email, one-page PDF, internal record. Use when the user says
6	  "/status-report", "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly
7	  update", "status update for Chris and Kenny", "what do I send Chris this week", or
8	  when a scheduled report date arrives. Do not use for a single meeting brief (use
9	  meeting-prep) or the end-of-day supervisor log interview (use interview-me).
10	---
11	
12	# Status Report
13	
14	Produce the recurring Applied Performance status report — an email to **Kenny Boyd and
15	Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly ("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), every two weeks, ~270 words.
16	
17	Governed by **KR 4.1** in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3). Read that KR as a
18	**content checklist** — shipped work, work in flight, decisions needed, anything at risk,
19	what's next — not as a layout. Eric's real reports run as flat prose with no section
20	headers. See **Voice** below; match it.
21	
22	**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish the email knowing what moved, what
23	needs them, and what's at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — visible involvement across
24	sports beyond football and basketball. That secondary job is why the report was asked
25	for; do not let it slip out of the output.
26	
27	**Design target: under 5 minutes of the user's time.** The machine does the recall. The
28	interview spends the user's attention only on what no system can know.
29	
30	## Paths
31	
32	Read `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` for all paths — never hardcode. Keys used
33	here: `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`,
34	`vault_status_reports`, `vault_status_log`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_scoreboard`,
35	`okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`, `canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`.
36	
37	Template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`
38	Output dir: `{vault_status_reports}`
39	
40	> Each machine has its own config: `config.windows.json` holds `C:\Users\eric_rash\...`
41	> paths (correct on Windows), `config.macos.json` holds `/Users/kristinarash/...` paths.
42	> Read the one for the machine you are on. If its values point at the *other* machine's
43	> layout, or `vault_root` does not exist, stop and fix the config first — every skill that
44	> trusts it is broken until you do. (Until 2026-08-11 a single config held stale Windows
45	> paths; the split per-platform configs replaced it.)
46	
47	## Relationship to other skills
48	
49	- **`weekly-review` is not a prerequisite.** Never require it to have run. If review
50	  files exist in `Inbox/weekly-review/` for the period, read them as a bonus input; if
51	  they don't, proceed without comment. The report builds from primary sources so it
52	  cannot inherit another ritual's failure rate.
53	- **`meeting-sync`** may be invoked to freshen the meeting corpus, but a sync failure is
54	  **not** a hard stop here — fall back to `fireflies-pp-cli digest` live, and note in the
55	  internal record that the vault copy was stale.
56	- **`html-to-pdf`** renders the one-pager.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Step 1 — Establish the period
61	
62	Read the newest file in `{vault_status_reports}`. Period start = the previous report's
63	`period_end`; period end = today. If no prior report exists, period start = 14 days ago.
64	
65	**Count sends.** KR 4.1's target is "≥3 **sent** by Aug 31," and writing a file is not
66	sending it. Count files in `{vault_status_reports}` with `sent: true` in frontmatter —
67	that is the real number. Report progress toward ≥3 in Step 8. If files exist with
68	`sent: false` older than a week, ask whether they actually went out; an uncounted send
69	is as bad for the KR as a missed one.
70	
71	A missed send widens the period rather than skipping it. Never leave a gap in the
72	archive — the archive's continuity is what makes it usable as a time record.
73	
74	**Cadence is settled: every two weeks.** Eric committed to it in writing in the first
75	report — "Starting these updates every two weeks." Report 1 went out **2026-08-24**, so
76	sends land on even fortnights from there (2026-09-07, 09-21, 10-05, …). The earlier
77	"twice monthly, 1st and 3rd Friday" plan was an assistant assumption and is retired.
78	
79	## Step 2 — Pull (no user involvement)
80	
81	### Step 2a — Preflight the meeting source
82	
83	Run `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5` first.
84	
85	**Fixed 2026-08-11** — the key is in `~/.zshrc` and the local mirror was rebuilt with
86	`fireflies-pp-cli sync`; as of 2026-08-13 the key is visible to the Bash tool directly.
87	The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`, not `~/.fireflies-pp-cli/`.
88	
89	If it fails again, `unable to open database file: out of memory (14)` means the mirror is
90	**missing, not corrupt** — run `sync` before anything else. Then:
91	
92	- **Do not hard-stop.** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure; this skill must not,
93	  or it inherits the outage that already lapsed `weekly-review`.
94	- **Fall back** to reading `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` filtered to the period by the
95	  `YYYY-MM-DD_` filename prefix. These files have **no YAML frontmatter** — parse the
96	  prepended header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) and the
97	  Fireflies export sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
98	- **Check staleness and say so.** Compare the newest meeting file's date to today. If
99	  the gap is >2 days, tell the user plainly in Step 8: *"Meeting data is stale through
100	  {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."* A silently incomplete
101	  report is worse than a flagged one — the user is about to send it to a supervisor.
102	- Record the degraded source in the internal record's frontmatter.
103	
104	### Step 2b — Pull
105	
106	Run these in parallel. Never ask the user for anything obtainable here.
107	
108	1. **Meetings** — `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent`
109	   (flags verified valid; `--since` accepts `7d`/`24h` form). Gives titles, gists,
110	   topics, and action items in one call. Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}`.
111	   On failure, use the 2a fallback.
112	1b. **Supervisor logs — read these before anything else.** Every file in
113	   `{vault_status_log}` whose `YYYY-MM-DD.md` filename falls inside the period. These are
114	   written by `closeout` Step 0 (or `interview-me` Part 0) and they are the **highest-value source in
115	   this step**: they cover equipment, installs, hallway conversations, and follow-ups
116	   awaiting a reply — the operational two thirds that appears in no other source. Merge
117	   the three sections (`## Equipment & installs`, `## People & conversations`,
118	   `## Waiting on / risks`) across the period and union every `sports:` array for the
119	   coverage panel.
120	
121	   Treat the wording as the user's own and preserve it. **Count the logged days** —
122	   `logged / days-in-period` gets reported in Step 8. A thin count is not a reason to
123	   pad; it is the number that tells the user the nightly ritual lapsed.
124	
125	   Zero logs is normal for now and is **never** a hard stop — the ritual started
126	   2026-09-07 and the report predates it. Fall back to a full Step 4 interview.
127	
128	2. **Commitments** — `{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent`
129	   (`--from` takes an integer number of days). Flag anything open >14 days; those are
130	   risk-section candidates. On failure, parse `## Action items` blocks from the vault
131	   meeting files instead.
132	
133	   **Known broken as of 2026-09-07:** this command exits 0 and returns an array of empty
134	   `{}` objects — a serialization bug, not an empty result. Do not read it as "no open
135	   commitments." The digest in item 1 carries action items inline; use those and record
136	   the degraded source in the internal record.
137	3. **Shipped artifacts** — read `{vault_output_ledger}`, newest first, entries within
138	   the period. **This is the only source for the "Shipped" section.**
139	
140	   Format is a markdown table, newest first, data rows starting at line 22:
141	   `| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |` where *Shipped* is `YYYY-MM-DD`,
142	   *Artifact* is the short name, *What it is* is a dense paragraph, and *Harvest* holds
143	   `[[wikilinks]]` or is empty. Match rows with `^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by
144	   date. Compress *What it is* to one clause for the email — those paragraphs run long
145	   and will blow the 300-word ceiling if pasted whole.
146	4. **Project movement** — read `{portfolio_json}`, filter `lane == "job"`. Use `stage`,
147	   `next_action`, and `updates[]` for the *In Progress* section only.
148	5. **KR state** — read `{okr_doc}` (v3, 14 KRs). This is the **only** trustworthy KR
149	   source. Two others will lie to you:
150	
151	   - **Never read the cadence doc's KR table** — superseded v2 set of 9.
152	   - **Do not trust `{okr_scoreboard}` for confidence values.** It was generated
153	     2026-06-12 against the retired *quarterly, 3-objective* set and scores KRs that no
154	     longer exist; v3's fourth objective (Leadership & Visibility) isn't in it at all.
155	     Its `Conf` decimals are real numbers attached to dead targets. If it still predates
156	     the v3 restructure (2026-07-17), tell the user it needs regenerating — `okrs.yaml`
157	     is the source of truth, `okr.py` regenerates `SCOREBOARD.md` and `okrs.json` — and
158	     report KR status from `{okr_doc}` alone in the meantime.
159	
160	6. **Sport roster** — the 17-program list for the coverage panel comes from
161	   `{utilization_brief}` §"Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the two XC / Track &
162	   Field rows each bundle two programs). Never re-derive this list from memory. Note it
163	   is *prescriptive* — what each program could use — not a record of current activity,
164	   which is exactly why the coverage panel is worth publishing.
165	7. **Canonical spine** — read `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` for the confirmed
166	   active list, each project's sport and KR mapping.
167	8. **Optional** — `Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` within the period, if any exist.
168	
169	### Hard rule: "Shipped" comes from the ledger, never from portfolio stage
170	
171	`portfolio.json` marks projects `stage: shipped` that still have stakeholder sign-off
172	outstanding — Sport_Tech_Vetting is currently `shipped` while KR 1.2 shows Chris's
173	sign-off pending. Reporting that as shipped tells the user's supervisor that a thing he
174	never approved is done. **Only `_ledger.md` entries qualify as Shipped.** Portfolio
175	stage feeds *In Progress*.
176	
177	## Voice — match the real thing, not the spec
178	
179	**Read `{vault_status_reports}/2026-08-24-email-sent.txt` before drafting.** That is the
180	first report Eric actually sent. It is the reference for how he writes; this skill's
181	earlier draft was never sent and should not be imitated.
182	
183	What his email actually does:
184	
185	- **No section headers.** Flat short paragraphs, one topic each, no Shipped / In Progress
186	  / Decisions Needed labels. Do not impose the KR 4.1 headers on his prose — they are the
187	  *content checklist*, not the layout. Make sure each of the five things is covered
188	  somewhere; do not label them.
189	- **One framing line up top**, then straight into it. No preamble.
190	- **"We" for department work, "I" for his own actions.** He writes as the unit.
191	- **Concrete and operational.** Equipment, buildings, people, dates: Perch cameras at
192	  Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar, survey cutoff August 28th. Names people
193	  freely — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi, Micah.
194	- **Asks come last and land soft:** "One ask I wanted to run past you both is whether…"
195	  Do **not** convert these into "need Chris by Aug 31." That register is more forceful
196	  than he writes and it will read as someone else's words.
197	- **Stalled things get passed along, not escalated:** "still haven't heard back. Passing
198	  that along in case a nudge is warranted."
199	- **About 270 words. No attachment.** The memo PDF exists for when something needs to be
200	  handed across a table; the ordinary cycle is email only.
201	
202	### The sourcing gap this exposed — important
203	
204	Almost nothing in his real report appears in `portfolio.json` or `_ledger.md`: survey
205	response rates, camera installs at three buildings, heart-rate monitors arriving for
206	tennis, staff meeting cadence, a stalled email to Micah. Those sources track his
207	**building** work. He reports his **departmental operations**.
208	
209	So the auto-pull covers maybe a third of what belongs in the report. **Weight the
210	interview accordingly** — ask about equipment, deliveries, installs, staffing, meetings
211	held, and follow-ups awaiting a reply, not just what moved in the registry. Treat a draft
212	built only from automated sources as roughly one-third finished.
213	
214	## Step 3 — Draft before asking
215	
216	Write a complete draft of all five sections from the pull. Cut to **5–6 projects with
217	real motion** — never a 14-line roster. Projects that didn't move go to the internal
218	record and, if relevant, the sport coverage panel.
219	
220	Tag every Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*,
221	*(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*, *(Cross-sport)*.
222	
223	Then identify the gaps — that is what the interview is for.
224	
225	## Step 4 — Interview the gaps only
226	
227	Ask in **one batch**, not serially. Keep it to what the pull genuinely couldn't answer.
228	Lead with targeted gap questions, then the four standing ones.
229	
230	**Targeted** (generated from the pull, examples):
231	- "Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything from them that Chris needs?"
232	- "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period — is that right, or did something go out
233	  that never got logged?"
234	- "Kinexon_Volleyball hasn't moved in the registry since July. Stalled, or just not
235	  logged?"
236	
237	**Skip every standing question the supervisor logs already answered.** If
238	`{vault_status_log}` covered the period, questions 1–4 below are largely pre-filled —
239	read the merged log back to the user as a list and ask only *"anything missing?"* plus
240	questions 5–8. Re-asking what the user already typed at 9pm is how the nightly ritual
241	gets abandoned; the payoff for logging has to be a visibly shorter interview.
242	
243	**Standing** (every time). The first three carry most of the report — they cover the
244	operational half no automated source sees:
245	
246	1. **Equipment, installs, deliveries.** What arrived, what got installed where, what's
247	   being phased out, who's onboarding onto it. Eric's real reports lead with this
248	   (Perch cameras at Fudge, FirstBeat monitors replacing Polar for tennis).
249	2. **Meetings held and staffing.** Who he met with, what came out of it, changes to
250	   cadence or who attends. Names matter — Linda, Noah, AJ, Javi.
251	3. **Conversations no transcript caught** — hallway, text, sideline, phone. Invisible to
252	   every automated source, and among the highest-value things this interview captures.
253	4. **Anything waiting on someone else.** Unanswered emails, pending approvals, stalled
254	   follow-ups. These become the soft "passing that along" lines at the end.
255	5. **Anything about to go sideways** that Chris and Kenny should hear from him first.
256	   *(Push here. An always-empty risk line means it isn't being used honestly.)*
257	6. **Any ask** — time at a meeting, a decision, a nudge. Phrased softly, at the end.
258	7. **Ideas generated** — worth parking, pitching, or building?
259	8. **What's next** for the coming two weeks.
260	
261	Also ask, if the pull shows thin coverage: *"Any sport you touched this period that
262	isn't showing up in my sources?"* Non-revenue involvement is the whole point and it is
263	the most likely thing to be undercounted.
264	
265	## Step 5 — Assemble and check
266	
267	Fill the template at `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`.
268	
269	Run every check before showing the user anything:
270	
271	- [ ] **Email body is under 300 words.** Count it. State the count. Over the ceiling,
272	      cut — do not negotiate with yourself.
273	- [ ] **Every Shipped line traces to a `_ledger.md` entry.** No exceptions.
274	- [ ] **No endorsement claimed that doesn't exist.** If sign-off is pending, "our
275	      standard intake process," never "the approved process."
276	- [ ] **Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag.**
277	- [ ] **Every Decisions Needed item names a person and a date.** No owner or no date
278	      means it isn't a decision request — rewrite or cut it.
279	- [ ] **Jargon table enforced.** No CMJ, ACWR, asymmetry index, unexplained B.A.I.R.
280	- [ ] **Department names.** Athletic Performance (not strength and conditioning / S&C),
281	      Athletic Medicine (not sports medicine), Applied Performance (not sport science).
282	- [ ] **Never "one unified dashboard."** The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke
283	      on top."
284	- [ ] **Research presented as research** — no readiness or deployment claims.
285	- [ ] **Risks section is non-empty** unless the user explicitly confirmed there's
286	      nothing. Ask once more before letting it go empty.
287	- [ ] **Repeat check:** any Decisions Needed item carried over from the previous report
288	      gets flagged to the user — two unanswered asks means the email has failed at it
289	      and it needs raising in person.
290	- [ ] **Email and PDF agree.** The two are filled separately, so verify it: every
291	      Shipped, In Progress, Decisions Needed, and Risks item in the email appears in the
292	      PDF. The PDF may carry *more* detail — it must never carry different facts, a
293	      different sport tag, or a different date. Sending a supervisor two versions of the
294	      same report is the failure this check exists to prevent.
295	- [ ] **Sport coverage panel is not padded.** Untouched sports stay marked untouched. A
296	      thin panel is real information; a padded one destroys the evidentiary value of
297	      every honest panel before and after it.
298	
299	**Loop until clean.** Any failed box: fix the draft, then run the whole list again from
300	the top — a cut for word count can drop a sport tag or the only risk line. Show the user
301	the draft only after one full pass with every box ticked.
302	
303	## Step 6 — Emit
304	
305	Produce three things:
306	
307	1. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record, full Layer 3
308	   structure from the template: email as sent, meetings held, conversations, ideas, full
309	   roster, KR ledger, and the "Not for the report" candid section.
310	2. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — render
311	   `assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content. One page, always.
312	
313	   **It is a printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Single column, one serif family,
314	   letterspaced small-cap section heads, one green hairline. Never reintroduce status
315	   dots, badge or pill rows, bolded stat lines, progress bars, or a two-column grid —
316	   that vocabulary is what made the first version read as generated.
317	
318	   **Measure before shipping**, don't eyeball it. Budget is **950px of content at 666px
319	   width**:
320	
321	   Same script on both machines (`python3` on the Mac, `python` on Windows); it finds
322	   Chrome and the temp folder itself:
323	
324	   ```python
325	   import pathlib, platform, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile
326	   html = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])            # the one-pager .html
327	   chrome = {"Darwin": "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome",
328	             "Windows": r"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"}[platform.system()]
329	   probe = pathlib.Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "probe.html"
330	   probe.write_text(html.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("</body>",
331	       '<script>window.addEventListener("load",()=>{document.title='
332	       '"H:"+Math.round(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)})</script></body>'),
333	       encoding="utf-8")
334	   dom = subprocess.run([chrome, "--headless", "--disable-gpu", "--virtual-time-budget=3000",
335	                         "--window-size=666,1200", "--dump-dom", probe.as_uri()],
336	                        capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8",
337	                        errors="replace").stdout   # Windows Python defaults to cp1252
338	   print(re.search(r"<title>H:(\d+)", dom).group(1), "px (budget 950)")
339	   ```
340	
341	   Then render with the same `chrome`: `--headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer
342	   --print-to-pdf=<out> <html file URI>` (or the `html-to-pdf` skill on Windows).
343	   Over 950px, **cut prose** — never drop below 9.6pt. This gets printed and read by
344	   people who will not squint for you.
345	3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
346	   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
347	   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
348	   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
349	   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
350	   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
351	4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
352	   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.
353	
354	### Do not send
355	
356	The connected Gmail account is the user's **personal** address
357	(`eric.rash11@gmail.com`), not Baylor. Do not create Gmail drafts — they would land in
358	the wrong mailbox. The user sends from Outlook on the work account.
359	
360	Never send a report to a supervisor without the user reading it first, under any
361	circumstance.
362	
363	## Step 7 — Log
364	
365	- Append shipped artifacts to `{vault_output_ledger}` if the interview surfaced any that
366	  weren't logged.
367	- Update `Applied-Performance-Active-Projects.md` with confirmed status, sport, and KR
368	  mapping — this keeps the canonical spine current as a byproduct rather than a chore.
369	- Add an `updates[]` entry to `{portfolio_json}` for each project reported as moved, via
370	  the `project` skill, so the registry stops being empty.
371	- Set `sent: false` in the internal record. The user flips it after sending.
372	
373	## Step 8 — Report to the user
374	
375	State: word count, report number, next send date, which sports appeared, anything the
376	checks flagged, and where the three files landed.
377	
378	Also state **`N of D` days logged** in `{vault_status_log}` for the period. Say it
379	plainly and without nagging — the number is the nudge. When the count is low, say what it
380	cost: *"6 of 14 days logged, so the interview had to cover the other 8 from memory."*
381	
382	**Propose a rule when one was missing.** If this run hit a problem no Step 5 box covers —
383	caught by you, or by Eric editing the draft before sending — end with one proposed new
384	checklist line and the reason. Add it to Step 5 only on Eric's yes; the next report is
385	then checked against it.
386	
387	---
388	
389	## Failure modes to design against
390	
391	**Padding.** A thin period is a legitimate output. "Nothing shipped this period" is an
392	honest line that protects the word "shipped" everywhere else. Inflating a quiet period
393	is the fastest way to make the report worthless — and to make the time documentation
394	inadmissible when it matters.
395	
396	**Roster creep.** The email is not a project list. 14 status lines reads as 14 things
397	half-done. Five moving projects reads as focus.
398	
399	**The credit goal quietly disappearing.** The report exists so non-football,
400	non-basketball involvement becomes visible. If a period's coverage panel is thin, that
401	is real information and it should be shown, not hidden — a padded panel destroys the
402	evidentiary value of every honest one.
403	
404	**Depending on another ritual.** `weekly-review` lapsed for seven weeks earlier this
405	year. This report must never require it.
406

`status-report` reads that folder first (Step 2b item 1b), skips standing interview

**Why:** roughly two thirds of what belongs in the supervisor email — equipment arriving,
installs, hallway conversations, follow-ups awaiting a reply — appears in **no** automated

departmental operations. A draft from automated sources alone is about one-third finished.

reflection is expensive when tired and this ritual already lapsed 49 days once. The
"N of D" count is the nudge; never backfill missing days to make it look better. Never
pad the log — `status-report` copies entries into an email to supervisors with light
editing, so an invented install becomes a false claim in front of Chris Ruf.

=== project_kenny-boyd-writing-voice
---
name: kenny-boyd-writing-voice
description: "How Kenny Boyd (Exec Sr Assoc AD, SA Services) writes and leads — post template, tics, bad-news pattern, what he values; use when writing to him, for him, or in his voice"
metadata:
