---

Source: SA Services Leadership channel export (19 agendas 9/2025–3/2026), 11 Teams
posts 3/27–10/5/2026, and 96 emails from Kenny to Eric (10/2025–10/5/2026), reviewed
2026-10-06.

**Two registers.** Agendas: bare outlines, two-sided slogans ("Thermostat vs.
Thermometer", "Anger vs. Apathy", "Be Present"), questions as prompts ("Why are we doing
___?"), a running "What I'm working on…" list repeated weekly. Posts: warm prose that
explains the reason for every ask.

**Post template.** Bold label-first title (PLEASE REVIEW: / ASSISTANCE NEEDED: /
REMINDER: / Article Review:), banner for big items → @team + one purpose sentence →
numbered asks to a role ("Unit Leads - Please…") → why → his travel/OOO dates → thanks.

**Tics.** Numbers in parentheses "(3) weeks", "(38)". Ellipses as hand-off ("Let us know
on this thread…"). Long sentences, typos left in — writes fast, substance over polish.
"We/us" by default; "I" when taking ownership. CAPS/bold only for rules with
consequences ("DO NOT PARK"). Light self-deprecating humor ("do forget (like I have)").

**Faith.** Woven in as allusion ("for such a time as this"), weekly Scripture + leadership
quote in fall 2025 agendas, "Spiritual Wellness day", prayer question in athlete survey.

**Bad-news pattern (4/30 Athletes.org post).** State headline neutrally → "dig into the
details" (asks sample size) → numbered context → concede ("We certainly can improve") →
name who owns it (Doug, Jovan, Dave Harper) → close on pride and mission. Defends team
without dismissing the criticism.

**Values.** Prep before meetings (bullets in advance). Lead time upward: internal
deadline well before the official one, so Doug/President have room. Explicit about who
sees what (Real Response access list). Good-neighbor framing; reframes constraints as
fortune. Protects staff time and well-being. Personnel requests go to him first, keep
him copied. Prefers subtraction over adding process. Skeptical of low-n surveys
("number of participants matter significantly").

**Email specifics.** Subject labels: FOR REVIEW / RESPONSE REQUESTED / PLEASE RESPOND
SEPARATELY / FEEDBACK REQUESTED. Says exactly how to reply (reply all, separately,
text). Closes loopholes in asks ("(3) challenges; if personnel is one, give (3)
others"). Acks are one line ("Received. Thank you"). Credits people by name, often
including partner offices ("would not have been possible without…"). Tailors one
announcement for different audiences. To vendors: courteous, states his authority, makes no commitment.
Hospitality is a core value ("Unreasonable Hospitality" book for new staff).

**With Eric specifically.** Assigns work as "Coach Rash," with a deliverable, a deadline
and his review window ("by EOD Friday so I can review over the weekend"), with constraints
stated up front. Replies "great starting point" and then edits it himself. Asks scoping
checks on numbers ("only health and wellness research?"). Wants documents going upward
formalized and comprehensive ("include ALL areas"), traceable to external standards
(map the NCAA Perf Tech components in an appendix), and fitting existing ITS/campus
workflows rather than parallel ones. Approves with conditions (get the coach and AT to
sign off) and always "keep me updated," especially on cross-office comms. Delegates
by relationship ("you can speak their language to ITS"). Since 10/1/26: weekly
30-minute project check-in with Eric through the fall.

**Spoken (Fireflies SA_Leadership_10052026).** Opens the meeting with a devotional tied to the
point in the semester (mid-semester "peaks and valleys", Psalm 121 + Wooden) and a
call for leaders to be "that calming force". Closes with a reflection and a spoken prayer. Talks
in long, circling sentences full of "you know / I think / kind of". Explains decisions
plainly ("I'll just say it plainly", e.g. BANC breakfast cut on budget and football
practice times). Key lines: "inviting feedback requires you to be prepared to act upon
it"; "if we're going to do it… say we're going to do it and say we did". He redirects new
initiatives into existing groups ("instead of adding something else"). Pulse: 82 =
17% participation; goal ~1/3; calls it "a trust building process"; warns that raw
survey data skews toward the disgruntled ("don't take it personally").
In small private groups he gets blunt and informal and sizes up stakeholders by how
he expects them to react. Databricks stance (10/5/26): sees it as possibly
the next step beyond Kitman; start with one team; bring in neutral interpreters
between the data and the sport; a per-sport "menu" of what data goes in; ROI including
NIL; willing to push from the top ("ignorance cannot be a reason to stop"). He grounds
Eric's enthusiasm ("get too carried away"); he's already sold on the vision and wants
governance, a small proof of concept and a plan for the people who resist.

**How to apply:** Writing to or for him, use his template; with bad news use his order
(context, concede, owner). Hit his internal deadline, not the official one. Don't
over-polish. Frame Applied Performance work against his five annual goals (11/10/25):
industry-leading division, campus partnership (the research team Eric leads), unit
leader development, service prioritization, student-athlete voice.

name: kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences
description: "Kenny Boyd's editorial constraints on Athletics policy/framework docs — no language implying past incompetence, no judgmental tier labels, name the seniority of reviewers"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 126c5de4-d928-4658-88d2-1922d2464a29
  modified: 2026-10-28T21:15:11.442Z
---

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

Format (his own words, Tech Sync 2026-10-28): no long wordy documents; "economy of
words"; a clean cover with the details behind it; charts and trend lines over
text ("not a pre-K version" either). Say plainly when something already exists
("we already have this") so work is not duplicated. To him "the SOP" means the
Software and Technology Management Framework.

**Why:** These are tone constraints, not content ones — the same facts land or
fail on phrasing. Getting them wrong costs a full review cycle.

**How to apply:** Before sending any Athletics policy or framework draft for his
review, scan for blame-implying rationale, ranking adjectives on process tiers,
and unqualified office names where seniority matters.

# HTML to PDF

Headless-Chrome render of a local HTML file to PDF. No manual browser printing.

## Quick start

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME\.claude\skills\html-to-pdf\scripts\html2pdf.ps1" -HtmlPath "report.html"
# optional explicit output:
#   ... -HtmlPath "report.html" -OutPdf "C:\path\coach-report.pdf"
```

Defaults: same folder, same name, `.pdf` extension. Report the output path and size to the user when done.

## Page setup lives in the HTML, not in flags

Headless Chrome takes page size/orientation from CSS `@page`. If the source lacks one, inject a style block before rendering (edit the file or a temp copy):

```html
<style>
  @page { size: Letter portrait; margin: 12mm; }        /* or: Letter landscape */
  body { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
</style>
```

- `print-color-adjust: exact` keeps background colors/graphics — the equivalent of ticking "Background graphics" in the print dialog. Coach-facing reports almost always need it.
- Landscape decks: `size: Letter landscape`. Slide decks sized in `vh/vw` may need a fixed pixel size instead, e.g. `@page { size: 1280px 720px; margin: 0; }`.

Copy between the rules. Paste into Outlook. Attach the PDF. Send from the Baylor account.

**To:** Chris Ruf

Chris — status through {{PERIOD_END_DATE}}. Kenny cc'd. One-pager attached.

**Decisions Needed**

**Risks / No Surprises**
- {{What slipped, went sideways, or is about to — and what I'm doing about it.}}

**Next Two Weeks**

- {{Priority 2}}

Full detail and sport coverage in the attachment.

— Eric

---

### Rules for the email

**300 words is a ceiling, not a target, and it is not negotiable.** Roughly 60 words a
section, two to three bullets each. The ceiling is the feature — it forces the email to
carry only what a supervisor can act on. Overflow goes to the PDF, never into the body.

**"Shipped" means an artifact exists that someone outside your head received.** Source
it from `SecondBrain/output/_ledger.md` only. **Never** from `portfolio.json`
`stage: shipped` — the registry currently marks Sport_Tech_Vetting as shipped while
KR 1.2 still shows Chris's sign-off outstanding. Telling Chris something shipped that
Chris hasn't approved is the single most damaging thing this report could do. If nothing
shipped, write "Nothing shipped this period." That line is legitimate and it protects
the credibility of every other time you use the word.

**Never claim an endorsement that doesn't exist.** If sign-off hasn't landed, write
"our standard intake process," not "the approved process." Carried over from the
stakeholder briefing plan; same rule applies here.

**Every "Decisions Needed" item names a person and a date.** A decision request without
an owner and a deadline is a complaint. This is the section Chris and Kenny should read
first, and it is what makes the email worth their time — it turns reporting into
unblocking. If two consecutive reports carry the same unanswered item, escalate it in
person; the email has already failed at it twice.

**"Risks / No Surprises" is where the report earns its keep.** Objective 4 says
leadership is never surprised. This section is how you spend that. Bad news goes here,

# Applied Performance — Unit OKRs (2026–27)

## Vision (North Star)
**Be the best applied performance department in the country.**

That's the bar. A KR is "done" only at a level a top-5 program would recognize, not just "we did a thing."

## Mission (how we get there)
Turn Baylor's athlete data into decisions that keep athletes available and performing, build the data and performance literacy of the people who use it, and produce original research that advances both the program and the university's R1 mission.

Three permanent **service pillars** — Data Systems & Analytics, Education, Research & Development — plus one **enabling objective** (Leadership & Visibility) that the new responsibilities document made explicit: the unit now delivers through people and process

**Eric's protected hands-on lanes** (not delegated, not reviewed-only — built by his hands): HPI protocol and its dashboarding; technology vetting; white-paper analysis; one-off report and dashboard creation for sports. Delegation stops at these boundaries.

## Sport coverage — the honest baseline

The report exists to make involvement across sports visible. The roster of programs
comes from `DEV/AppliedUtilization/Applied_Performance_Utilization_Brief.md`
§"Recommendations by program" — 15 rows covering all 17 varsity programs. That document
is **prescriptive** (what each program *could* use), not a record of activity. Measured
against evidence, here is where things actually stand:

### `update <name> <note>`
`add-update "<name>" "<note>"`, plus `--next-action "<step>"` when Eric gave one.

### `start` / `park` / `done <name>`
`set-status "<name>" active|paused|done`, with `--note` when Eric gave a reason. Starting a
`job`, `side` or `tool` row with no `receiver`: ask Eric who it is for, then run
`set-receiver` with his words (`me: <why>` when it is for himself).

### `stage <name> <stage>`
`set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`. When the stage is `shipped`, offer once: "Want me to run
/harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On
yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that project.

### `promote <idea>` and `rank`
Both change the registry where no CLI command reaches: follow
[`REGISTRY-EDITS.md`](REGISTRY-EDITS.md). Dragging cards on the board re-ranks faster.

### bare `/project`
Run `board.py --background` and give the URL. Waiting ideas are the board's Inbox column.

## After a change

The board picks up registry changes on its next poll (a few seconds); there is nothing to
render. Tell Eric in one line what changed. Closeout commits the registry as
`data: board edits <date>`, so leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted unless Eric asks.

Delete a project or idea only after Eric confirms that exact row.

**Done when:** the command printed its success line (or the hand edit saved and the
`.bak` beside `portfolio.json` was refreshed), and Eric has the one-line summary.

  read the Fireflies sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).

conversations and follow-ups awaiting a reply appear nowhere else.

  period; union every `sports:` array for the coverage panel.

  nightly ritual lapsed. Never pad it. (2026-10-31: three logs exist, 09-07 to 09-14.)
- Zero logs never stops the run; Step 4 then covers everything.

the email.

`portfolio.json` `stage: shipped` is not evidence: it marks projects shipped while stakeholder sign-off is
outstanding (Sport_Tech_Vetting was `shipped` while KR 1.2 showed Chris's sign-off pending). Stage feeds
In Progress only.

Use `next_action` and `updates[]` (`date`, `note`). `stage` is empty on most rows and `charter` exists on
a few, so lean on `updates[]`. Also read `{canonical_projects}` for each project's sport and KR.

The registry holds Eric's building work. A draft from the automated sources alone is about one third of
the report; the interview supplies the rest.

`Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` is the only KR source. Its current cycle is Fall 2026 (7 KRs, written
2026-09-14). Report KR status from that file alone.

The 17 varsity programs come from `{utilization_brief}` section "Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the
two XC / Track & Field rows each bundle two programs), and `{canonical_projects}` section "Sport
coverage" holds the evidence baseline. Read both; never list programs from memory. The brief says what each
program could use, so it is a roster and the coverage panel is the activity record.

`{vault_root}/Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` inside the period, when present. The report never waits on it.

---
name: status-report
description: >-
  Build the every-two-weeks Applied Performance status report for Kenny Boyd and Chris
  Ruf — paste-ready email, one-page PDF, internal record. Use when the user says
  "/status-report", "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly
  update", "status update for Chris and Kenny", "what do I send Chris this week", or
  when a scheduled report date arrives. Do not use for a single meeting brief (use
  meeting-prep) or the end-of-day supervisor log interview (use interview-me).
---

# Status Report

The recurring Applied Performance email to **Kenny Boyd and Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly
("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), about 270 words, with a one-page PDF and an internal record. Governed by **KR 4.1**
in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md`, read as a content checklist: shipped work, work in flight,
decisions needed, anything at risk, what's next.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish knowing what moved, what needs them, and what is at
risk. **Secondary job: credit** for work across sports beyond football and basketball; that is why the
report exists, so the sport tags and the coverage panel stay in every cycle.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of Eric's time.** The machine does the recall; the interview spends
his attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Keys come from `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (`macos` or `windows`, whichever
machine this is): `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`, `vault_status_reports`,
`vault_status_log`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`,
`canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`. When `vault_root` does not exist, the config belongs to the other
machine: stop and fix it first.

Record template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`, **Layer 2 and Layer 3 only**. Its Layer 1 (headed
sections, "Chris —" greeting, attached PDF) is the old layout; the email follows **Voice** below.

`weekly-review` is never a prerequisite. `html-to-pdf` is not needed: `scripts/onepager_pdf.py` renders.

## Step 1 — Establish the period

1. **Prior report** = the newest `*-status.md` in `{vault_status_reports}` (the folder also holds drafts,
   PDFs and HTML). Period start = its `period_end`; period end = today. With no prior record, start = 14
   days ago. Report number = prior `report_number` + 1.
2. **Missed fortnights widen the period.** The archive never has a gap.
3. **Sent or not.** A report counts as sent when its record says `sent: true` or its folder holds
   `YYYY-MM-DD-email-sent.txt`. When the prior report has neither, add "did report N go out?" to the
   Step 4 batch; an unconfirmed report stays unsent.
4. **Send dates** fall every 14 days from 2026-08-24 (the first send, "Starting these updates every two
   weeks"): 2026-11-02, 11-16, 11-30, 12-14. The last is 12-14; the semester closes 12-18.
